texts.facts: The Ld. Trial Court vide impugned judgment dated 12.05.2017 had convicted the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) read with Section 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration (hereinafter referred as PFA) Act and vide order dated 18.05.2017, sentenced appellant no. 1 to undergo SI for one year with fine of Rs. 50,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) read with Section 7 of PFA Act and to Mahinder Kumar Khandelwal And Oth vs State on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41663703/ The complaint was then filed in the court on 15.05.2006 u/s 2(ia)(a), (b), (c) and (m) of PFA Act r/w Rule 44(c) of PFA Rules. On the basis of the PA report, notice of accusation u/s 251 Cr.P.C. was framed against the appellants u/s 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of Section 2(ia)(a), (b), (c) and (m) of PFA Act and Rule 44(c) of PFA Rules to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. None of the appellants lead any evidence in defence despite opportunity. a. That the judgment of Ld. Trial Court is based on prediction and assumptions and suffers from errors of law and appreciation of evidence. Since the presence of food inspector is doubtful, therefore the proceedings u/s 7/16 PFA cannot be maintained and are liable to be dismissed That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that there were public persons and police personnel available at the spot on 13.09.2005 but none of them were joined during investigation.
